body: The Mark of Kri is San Diego Studio's PlayStation 2 action-adventure, released in North America on 30 July 2002. Rau, a powerful young warrior, accepts assignments that lead him into a larger danger involving a divided magical mark. His bird companion Kuzo scouts ahead through a fantasy world influenced by Polynesian imagery. The broad character shapes and animated presentation contrast with the severity of the combat. Encounters mix direct fighting with opportunities to observe an area and quietly remove guards before the whole group responds.

Sweeping the right stick across nearby enemies assigns each selected target a controller button. Pressing the corresponding button directs Rau's attack toward that opponent, allowing him to deal with threats surrounding him. This separates choosing whom to strike from moving the warrior, making the rhythm of a group fight easier to follow. Weapons change the reach and character of those encounters. The player can also approach unseen, using stealth attacks to reduce the number of enemies before a more open battle becomes necessary.

Kuzo provides a view of places Rau has not yet reached, helping the player identify guards and possible approaches. The companion therefore supports the same attention to positioning that shapes the fighting system. Former two-dimensional animators contributed to the game's visual character, while Jack Wall's adaptive score responded closely to changes in the action. Its combination of scouting, stealth and unusual targeting gave a familiar warrior adventure a distinctive feel. Rise of the Kasai followed in 2005, developed by BottleRocket Entertainment after members of the original team moved there.
